front: The six parts of a forecasting design answer?
back: Requirements and decision, data and features, models and baselines, evaluation, serving and scale, monitoring and failure modes.

front: Why size the problem with numbers?
back: Series count, rows and compute time decide if you need a global model, parallel jobs, or sampling.
Observed sales are lower than real demand because the item was out of stock. Training on it makes forecasts too low.

front: When use quantile forecasts for ordering?
back: When over- and under-stock costs differ. Order at the quantile equal to under-cost divided by the sum of both costs.
Late data, a missing promotion entry, a new product without history. Also holiday shifts and stock-outs.

front: What is a good fallback forecast?
back: Seasonal naive or the last good forecast. It keeps the system working when data or models fail.
Backtest estimates forecast error on history. An A/B test measures the business effect, such as waste and stock-outs.
